sub_scenario.family: travel recovery physiology versus high-stakes scheduling
sub_scenario.one_line: global account director: the red-eye pattern already cost a signed error

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the deal review file and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The travel folio review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Daytime flights, even long ones, leave my next morning fully intact.
Daytime travel is free.
Effectively free, yes.
Someone new shadowed me in the account team channel this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the contract terms into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

The morning after the Frankfurt red-eye I ran the deal review flat and signed off a pricing error that took two amendment cycles to unwind; my own travel log flags every overnight eastbound the same way.
The log makes the pattern personal and specific.
Specific to overnight eastbound, every time.
Red-eyes before light days are absorbable; I schedule recovery and lose nothing.
Recovery scheduling absorbs the cost.
When there is room to schedule it, always.
I archived last cycle's notes on the travel folio and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My sleep specialist confirmed the pattern: overnight eastbound flights suppress my next-day executive function regardless of how I feel.
Clinically confirmed, not anecdotal.
Confirmed and documented.
A vendor call about the deal review file ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the account team channel checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the contract terms.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the travel folio records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The Tokyo signing is calendared for the morning after the only direct overnight flight; the alternative is departing Thursday, two hotel nights earlier, arriving with a full recovery day.
The calendar sets up the exact hazard.
The exact one in my log.
I sketched next week's plan for the contract terms before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the deal review file updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The signing includes final price-term confirmation on the spot; it is precisely the dense-detail work the flat mornings corrupt.
The task profile matches the vulnerability.
Matches it point for point.
I compared two options for the travel folio tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the account team channel handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
I booked the Thursday departure with two extra hotel nights instead of the Sunday red-eye, and my vice president questioned the cost. What in my record justifies the booking?
